statement: Let H=K_{1,3} disjoint-union K_2, with copies understood as ordinary (not necessarily induced) subgraphs. Every red-blue edge-colouring of every finite simple maximal planar graph G with |V(G)| at least 21 contains a monochromatic copy of H. Equivalently, P(21) holds and r_MP(H,H) exists with r_MP(H,H) at most 21. No claim is made that 21 is the least threshold.
contribution: The exact claw-cover dichotomy yields a uniform finite upper bound for the source-grounded disconnected singleton: mixed L/C avoiding colourings have order at most 16, while C/C avoiding colourings have order at most 20 by a planar bipartite count. This settles existence but not the least Ramsey threshold. The cited paper poses the broader disconnected classification and does not state this singleton separately; a limited current search found no equivalent primary result, which is not a priority claim.
